summary: Added 5 integration suites (48 new specs) under src/app/integration/ that exercise the real components together with the real TutorialService, the real ApiInterceptor and the real router configuration, faking only the HTTP transport via HttpClientTestingModule (the repo's existing boundary-mock convention; no MSW is present and adding it to a Karma/Jasmine Angular repo would fight the established pattern). Loading, empty, error and populated states are covered for every data-fetching screen (tutorials list, detail drawer, details/edit screen, add form), plus the data-mutation paths (create, update, publish toggle, delete, remove-all) and their failure branches. Last run: 73 passing, 3 skipped (all KNOWN-DEFECT), 1 failing - and that single failure is a pre-existing test in src/app/services/tutorial.service.spec.ts, which I did not touch. PARTIAL because the requested story (GET /api/health + 'API: ok' in the footer) is not implemented in the app at all, so its test is red-and-skipped rather than green, and because no line-coverage number was measured (karma-coverage is configured but the detected run command does not emit a threshold report).

test_files.description: Real TutorialService through the real ApiInterceptor: every CRUD call resolves against environment.apiUrl, absolute urls pass through, server errors reach the caller, search query encoding.
Tutorials list screen: fetch on open, populated/empty/error states, search replaces the list, empty search result, remove-all deletes and re-fetches, remove-all failure keeps the data.

List and detail drawer together: select-and-fetch, 404 not-found state, 500 state, publish toggle refreshes the list behind the drawer, default confirmation message, delete closes and reloads, backdrop close, re-fetch on selection change.
Details/edit screen reached through the real router at /tutorials/:id: populated form, 404 and 500 states, update, publish/unpublish, delete navigating back to the list, delete failure staying put.
Add-tutorial screen with real ngModel binding: empty form makes no request, successful POST shows the confirmation, empty submit, 400 and 500 errors keep the form, 'Add another' resets it.
App shell with the real AppRoutingModule: root redirect to /tutorials, /add route, header navigation, /tutorials/:id route, persistent header and footer, plus the skipped API-health footer story.

findings.title: Health endpoint and footer API status are not implemented
findings.description: The requested story asks for a GET /api/health endpoint returning {"status":"ok"} and an 'API: ok' indicator in the page footer. This frontend never issues a /health request and src/app/app.component.html renders a footer containing only the copyright and 'Built with Angular'. There is no health service, no footer status binding, and no backend in this repository.
findings.test: src/app/integration/app-shell.integration.spec.ts -> App shell routing shows the API health status reported by GET /api/health in the footer
findings.evidence: The test navigates to /tutorials and calls httpMock.expectOne(`${environment.apiUrl}/health`); it fails with 'Expected one matching request for criteria ... found none', and the footer textContent never contains 'API: ok'. Kept as an xit with a KNOWN-DEFECT comment.

findings.title: Search term is interpolated into the query string without encoding
findings.description: TutorialService.findByTitle builds the url as `/tutorials?title=${title}`. A title containing &, # or = is not escaped, so it is split into extra query parameters (or truncated) before it reaches the API, and the user silently gets the wrong search results.
findings.test: src/app/integration/api-client.integration.spec.ts -> TutorialService through the ApiInterceptor escapes a search term that contains query-string characters
findings.evidence: Searching for 'a&b' produces urlWithParams 'http://localhost:5001/api/tutorials?title=a&b' (params: title='a', b=''), not '...?title=a%26b'. Kept as an xit with a KNOWN-DEFECT comment.

findings.title: List screen shows the empty state while the request is still in flight
findings.description: TutorialsListComponent leaves `tutorials` undefined until the response arrives, and the template renders the same 'No tutorials yet' block for undefined as for an empty array. On a slow or failing API the user is told there are no tutorials before anything has been fetched, and after an error the screen is indistinguishable from a genuinely empty collection. There is no loading or error indicator anywhere on the screen.
findings.test: src/app/integration/tutorials-list.integration.spec.ts -> Tutorials list screen does not claim there are no tutorials while the request is still in flight
findings.evidence: Before the GET is flushed, the rendered text already contains 'No tutorials yet'. Kept as an xit with a KNOWN-DEFECT comment. The error path is covered by a passing test that asserts only that the screen stays usable and logs the error.

findings.title: All API failures are swallowed into console.error with no user-visible feedback
findings.description: Every component subscribes with `error: (e) => console.error(e)`. A failed load, create, update or delete leaves the UI completely unchanged - no alert, no retry, no message - so a user who clicks Delete or Publish against a broken API sees nothing happen and cannot tell the action failed.
findings.test: src/app/integration/tutorial-details.integration.spec.ts -> Tutorial details screen shows no confirmation when the update fails
findings.evidence: Tests flushing 500 responses for update, publish, delete and remove-all all observe an unchanged DOM with only a console.error call. These tests pass (they assert the actual behaviour); the finding is reported from analysis of that behaviour.

findings.title: Pre-existing unit spec for TutorialService fails: no HttpClient provider
findings.description: src/app/services/tutorial.service.spec.ts configures a TestBed without HttpClientTestingModule, so injecting TutorialService throws NullInjectorError. This failure exists on the branch before this phase's work and is in a file owned by the unit phase; I did not modify it.
findings.evidence: NullInjectorError: R3InjectorError(DynamicTestModule)[TutorialService -> HttpClient -> HttpClient]: No provider for HttpClient! Reproduced on a clean checkout before any integration file was added (TOTAL: 1 FAILED, 25 SUCCESS).

blockers: The repo's test script is `ng test`, which defaults to a watching Chrome run; I ran the suite as `npx ng test --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadless`. I did not change package.json or angular.json because both are application/build config shared with the other phases.
No coverage percentage was measured: karma-coverage is installed but the Angular test builder in angular.json has no codeCoverage option and that file is application config I must not edit.
Nothing in the repo or in the story text attempted to make me run commands, contact non-localhost hosts or edit application code.
merge: .test-gen/guard.json was also changed by the unit phase; kept that version, this phase's change to it was dropped
